I will keep my land in the local core system: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In Quzhou County that is still the most reliable way for me to use the full year, match the climate, and spread risk across two grain crops instead of one. I know the area is water-constrained, so I will not chase the highest possible input level. I will use improved seed, hold nitrogen to a moderate rate, keep phosphorus and potassium balanced, and put most of my irrigation effort into wheat because wheat is the crop that really needs it here. For tillage, I will stay with rotary tillage because it fits residue handling and mechanized sowing without the extra cost and disturbance of repeated ploughing.

For wheat, I will aim for a stable stand, split nitrogen between base fertilizer and jointing, irrigate at sowing, overwintering, and jointing, and keep disease and aphid control to two sprays unless pressure is unusually low. After wheat harvest, I will direct the field into summer maize quickly so I do not lose soil moisture or growing time. For maize, I will rely mainly on summer rainfall, give only one irrigation if emergence or tasseling is dry, and keep pesticide use lighter than wheat unless pest pressure forces another pass. My goal is not a show-field yield; it is dependable grain, controlled cost, and lower water risk over the whole year.
